target.title: feat(github-copilot): add native web search for Copilot GPT models
target.body:
Closes #78573

## What Problem This Solves

GitHub Copilot Responses models can use hosted web search, but OpenClaw only exposed the managed `web_search` path, so users needed another search provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copilot catalog entries from OpenAI or Azure OpenAI that advertise Responses and tool calls now carry `nativeWebSearchTool`. The Copilot wrapper uses native `web_search` only for that capability and only when no managed provider is pinned. Other models keep the existing route. No OpenAI, core, or public Plugin SDK changes.

## User Impact

Supported Copilot models can search the web through the user's Copilot subscription. Explicit managed providers, tool policy, and unsupported models behave as before.

## Evidence

Exact head `ea63ab2afc` was run through the real Copilot provider wrapper and streaming Responses transport without starting the Gateway:

```text
native          tool=web_search          effort=low     http=200 terminal=stop citation=www.weather.gov
brave pinned    tool=function:web_search effort=minimal
policy denied   tool=function:web_search effort=minimal
no capability   tool=function:web_search effort=minimal
```

A current Copilot catalog probe completed `web_search_call` for all 9 OpenAI-family Responses models tested: `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5.3-codex`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, `gpt-5.4-nano`, `gpt-5.5`, and the three `gpt-5.6` variants. `gpt-5-mini` and `gpt-5.5` returned `url_citation` output.

target.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #99054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users who remove a personal app/bot and later add it again can continue the same OpenClaw server-side DM session, allowing the bot to use prior conversation context after an app lifecycle boundary.

This targets Teams app-management lifecycle signals that the bot can actually observe. Live capture showed Teams' local "Remove chat history" action can arrive later as an ordinary message in the same personal `conversation.id`, with no `installationUpdate`, `conversationUpdate`, `membersAdded`, or `membersRemoved` activity. This PR does not claim to detect that fully local clear-chat action when Teams gives the bot no lifecycle or conversation-boundary signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams now routes `installationUpdate` removal activities and bot `membersRemoved` conversation updates into a lifecycle handler. On a removal boundary, the handler removes the cached Teams conversation reference, rotates the matching OpenClaw session entry to a new session id with `updatedAt: 0`, and clears provider-owned route/delivery/origin metadata so the next inbound message cannot resume the removed chat transcript.

The handler also treats a personal `installationUpdate action=add` as a reinstall boundary only when an existing route-matched Teams DM session is already active. That catches tenants or flows where the re-add signal is visible but the prior remove signal was missed, without resetting first-time installs. Finally, inbound personal DMs check for a stored same-user/same-bot conversation reference with a different Teams `conversation.id`; when Teams exposes that boundary, OpenClaw removes the previous reference and rotates the DM session.

## User Impact

After a true Teams app removal and re-add, the next inbound message starts from a fresh OpenClaw session instead of silently resuming prior DM or channel context. Operators also avoid retaining a cached proactive-send reference for the removed Teams conversation.

For Teams clear-chat/reopen flows, the patch protects the observable case where Teams gives the bot a new personal conversation id. If Teams reuses the same server-side conversation id and sends no lifecycle event, there is no bot-visible signal in the captured payloads; that remains a Teams platform limitation rather than a claim made by this PR.

Existing welcome-card behavior, normal messages, reactions, and unrelated lifecycle events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live corrected Dale smoke:
  - Baseline before app removal used a synthetic marker.
  - Teams app removal emitted `installationUpdate action=remove`.
  - Handler logged `msteams lifecycle remove handled`, `reason=installation-remove`, `conversationType=personal`, `conversationRemoved=true`, `sessionsReset=1`.
  - The session entry rotated to a new redacted session id with `updatedAt: 0` and no Teams route/delivery/origin metadata.
  - After re-add, Teams showed the welcome card and the verification prompt used a fresh session; the bot did not recall the pre-removal marker.
- Live Teams `Remove chat history` follow-up after deploying this branch:
  - Sent a synthetic pre-clear marker.
  - Used Teams `Remove chat history`, opened the app/chat again, and sent a verification prompt.
  - No `installationUpdate add`, lifecycle/remove activity, or DM conversation-boundary handler log appeared.
  - The same OpenClaw session id remained active, and the bot could recall the pre-clear marker.
  - This confirms the PR should not claim to fix Teams local clear-history behavior when Teams sends no lifecycle event and reuses the same server-side conversation id.
- Added regression coverage for:
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove`
  - personal `installationUpdate/remove-upgrade`
  - first-install `installationUpdate/add` with no active session
  - personal `installationUpdate/add` when an existing session is active
  - ignored channel `installationUpdate/add`
  - channel bot `membersRemoved`
  - ignored non-bot `membersRemoved`
  - race-safe session rotation
  - personal DM conversation-id boundary rotation
  - no rotation for matching personal conversation ids
  - no rotation for different stored bot ids
- Added monitor-level coverage proving the Teams activity shim dispatches `installationUpdate` and `membersRemoved` activities to registered lifecycle handlers.
- Validation:
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts` - 11 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.authz.test.ts` - 18 tests passed.
  - `pnpm test extensions/msteams` - 71 files passed, 1007 tests passed.
  - `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` - passed.
  - `pnpm format:check extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/lifecycle-handler.test.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.ts` - passed.
  - `git diff --check` - passed.



---

Migration note: This PR replaces #100371 with the same published head commit, moved from `spinen/openclaw` to `jimmypuckett/openclaw` so OpenClaw maintainers and repository automation can update the contribution without transferring authorship. Prior review, proof, and CI history remain available on #100371.

target.title: fix(macos): make onboarding advance with Return
target.body:
Related: #104424

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting macOS onboarding could see a highlighted Next button that ignored plain Return, and where a fresh packaged app reported source-checkout build instructions when the CLI was not installed yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

The onboarding action now uses SwiftUI's default-action shortcut, which maps plain Return rather than the KeyEquivalent overload's default Command modifier. Missing-CLI failures now explain both valid recovery paths: install the CLI, or build an actual source checkout.

## User Impact

Keyboard users can advance onboarding with Return. Fresh packaged-app failures give an accurate, copyable remediation instead of implying the app bundle itself needs `pnpm build`.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both symptoms from the signed exact-landed macOS app on a pristine Parallels snapshot.
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter CommandResolverTests` — 25 tests passed.
- `swiftlint lint --strict --config config/swiftlint.yml ...` — 0 violations across the three touched files.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): derive heap thresholds from V8 heap size limit (#104631)
target.body:
Closes #104631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` above the default (e.g. 8 GB on a 15 GB RAM host) receive false-positive `heap_threshold` critical memory pressure diagnostics as soon as `heapUsedBytes` reaches 2 GB, even when the V8 heap limit has 75%+ headroom and the system has abundant free memory.

This triggers unnecessary diagnostic events, log noise, and stability bundle writes, and can cause downstream monitoring or supervisor restart chains (the linked issue reports a gateway drain-and-restart sequence on the reporter's setup).

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic memory classifier previously hardcoded heap pressure thresholds at 1 GiB (warning) and 2 GiB (critical) — values that were reasonable for Node's default `--max-old-space-size` (~2 GB server / ~4 GB desktop) but do not scale when operators configure a larger heap limit.

This change derives default heap warning and critical thresholds from V8's effective `heap_size_limit`, so they automatically adapt to whatever `--max-old-space-size` is set:

- **Critical**: 75% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 2 GiB
- **Warning**: 60% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 1 GiB

The conservative lower bounds ensure small-heap or default-heap environments remain equally protected. RSS threshold and RSS growth detection are unchanged. No configuration key is added — the fix is fully automatic.

## User Impact

Users on decently-provisioned hosts (e.g. `--max-old-space-size=8192`) no longer see spurious `heap_threshold` critical pressure from routine heap usage at 2 GB, while the same protection level is preserved for default or constrained heap sizes. The change is invisible to operators: no new config, no migration, no restart requirement beyond the usual update.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (3 new, 14 total, all passing — the 3 diagnostic test suites total 99/99):

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `default heap thresholds never go below the original constants as a conservative lower bound (#104631)` | Adaptive defaults floor at 1 GiB / 2 GiB — small-heap protection unchanged |
| `emits heap_threshold at the adaptive default warning threshold (#104631)` | Warning fires at 60% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |
| `emits heap_threshold critical at the adaptive default critical threshold (#104631)` | Critical fires at 75% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |

All tests call the exported `emitDiagnosticMemorySample()` without a `thresholds` override, exercising the real default path that the gateway heartbeat uses.

**Real-behavior proof** (standalone harness, calling the same production `emitDiagnosticMemorySample` path):

Default V8 heap limit (~4.19 GB):

```
                                    OLD (hardcoded)                  NEW (adaptive)
heapUsed=1.50 GB  →  warning/heap_threshold @ 1 GB     no pressure
heapUsed=2.00 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    no pressure
heapUsed=2.50 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    no pressure
heapUsed=2.98 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    warning @ 2.51 GB
heapUsed=3.14 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    critical @ 3.14 GB
heapUsed=3.45 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    critical @ 3.14 GB
```

Enlarged heap limit (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, ~8.19 GB):

```
                                    OLD (hardcoded)                  NEW (adaptive)
heapUsed=1.50 GB  →  warning/heap_threshold @ 1 GB     no pressure
heapUsed=2.00 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    no pressure         ← false positive gone
heapUsed=2.50 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    no pressure
heapUsed=5.83 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    warning @ 4.91 GB
heapUsed=6.14 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    critical @ 6.14 GB
heapUsed=6.75 GB  →  critical/heap_threshold @ 2 GB    critical @ 6.14 GB
```

The output confirms:

1. The 2 GB false-positive `critical/heap_threshold` is eliminated on both default and enlarged heaps
2. Warning and critical events still fire at the correct proportional headroom (60%/75% of the V8 limit)
3. The fix scales correctly with `--max-old-space-size`, matching the reporter's environment

**Typecheck**: `tsgo:core` passes clean.

**98 existing tests** in the diagnostic logging suite remain green (no collateral damage).

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): keep telegram QA progress detail truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab Telegram live progress output can contain malformed text when a detail message has emoji at the 240-character truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bounded Telegram QA progress detail strings now use the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper. The existing code-unit limit remains unchanged; this only backs a cut up to avoid splitting an emoji surrogate pair. No progress format, output prefix, or scenario behavior outside truncation changes.

## User Impact

Telegram QA progress details remain well-formed when scenario or canary diagnostics contain long emoji-containing values.

## Evidence

### Regression test crosses the actual cut
The test now uses a 236-code-unit ASCII prefix followed by emoji+after. With this input the emoji surrogate pair spans indices [236, 237] and current main raw `.slice(0, 237)` keeps only the high surrogate — the test **fails** on current main. The fixed path uses `truncateUtf16Safe(sanitized, 237)` which detects the split surrogate pair and backs up to index 236, producing 236 `a` chars + `...` (239 code units) with no lone surrogate.

### Terminal behavior proof (before vs. after)

**Before fix** (current main, raw `.slice(0, 237)`):
- Truncated: 236 `a` + lone high surrogate (U+D83D at index 236)
- Final output: 236 `a` + lone surrogate + `...` (240 code units)
- Lone surrogate detected: **yes** — emoji rendering breaks

**After fix** (`truncateUtf16Safe`):
- Truncated: 236 `a` (backed up to avoid splitting surrogate pair)
- Final output: 236 `a` + `...` (239 code units)
- Lone surrogate detected: **no** — emoji preserved cleanly

```

✓ 45/45 passed

target.title: fix: Slack drops attachments delivered via message_changed file_share events
target.body:
Related: #28834

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users posting a Slack message with attached files — especially multiple documents — would have the attachments silently ignored when Slack delivered the upload as a `message_changed` event instead of a plain `message`.

Slack finalizes file uploads asynchronously: a post with several attachments frequently reaches the app as a bare message first (incomplete or empty `files`), with the complete file set arriving moments later inside a `message_changed` event whose inner message carries subtype `file_share`. Today that event is routed to the system-event path as a generic "Slack message edited" note, so the agent never sees the documents. Users get either no reply or a reply that ignores their files, with no error anywhere.

We hit this in production (a purchasing workflow where vendors' packing slips are posted to a channel as multi-file messages) and have been running this fix as a local patch since April.

## Why This Change Was Made

`registerSlackMessageEvents` now promotes a `message_changed` event back into the regular message pipeline **only** when it is a genuine content delivery: the inner message is user-authored (never self/bot-attributed), carries subtype `file_share` (or none), and actually delivers new content relative to `previous_message` (file set changed, text appeared where there was none, or text changed alongside files). Everything else — plain edits, deletions, self-attributed changes — keeps the existing system-event behavior, so the duplicate-reply regression class from #28834 is not reintroduced. The promoted event reuses the original message `ts`, so the existing seen-message dedupe still applies if the original message event was already processed.

## User Impact

Slack users can attach one or many files to a message and the agent reliably receives all of them, regardless of whether Slack delivers the upload synchronously or via a follow-up `message_changed`. Plain message edits still do not re-trigger agent replies.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/messages.test.ts`:
  - a user `file_share` `message_changed` with a new file set is promoted into the message pipeline (correct channel/user/ts and both files present) and does **not** enqueue a system event;
  - a plain text-edit `message_changed` still goes to the system-event path (regression guard for #28834);
  - an unchanged file set is **not** promoted;
  - self-attributed (bot-authored) `file_share` changes are **not** promoted.
- The same logic (originally patched into the bundled dist of 2026.4.10) has been running in a production Slack workspace since April 2026, where multi-document vendor posts previously never reached the agent and now do.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: fix(telegram): silently skip empty-text sends
target.body:
Supersedes #59725 (auto-closed by the 10-open-PR cap; not reopenable because the close `stateReason` is `COMPLETED` and the branch was force-pushed since). ## Scope note: re-derived on top of current main Most of the original branch scope has since landed on `main` through other work, so this PR was reset onto `main` and re-implemented to cover only the residual gaps: - #56620 added `filterEmptyTelegramTextChunks` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.replies.ts`), which already drops whitespace-only chunks before any send. - The `sendTelegramText` rewrite around `sendPlainFallback` / `buildTelegramPlainFallbackPlan` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts`) already recovers formatted-send failures when a non-empty plain fallback exists. - #93279 introduced the default-vs-rich delivery split, which this PR preserves: the rich lane stays opt-in behind `richMessages === true` and both lanes get the same skip semantics. Two gaps remain on current `main`, and they are exactly the reported user path: 1. `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` only matches Telegram's legacy `message text is empty` wording. The live Bot API now also returns `text must be non-empty` (raw round-trip below), so the empty-text 400 escapes the recovery branch. 2. When non-whitespace source renders to empty visible text and the plain fallback is also empty (for example `` with `plainText: ""`), `main` throws (`empty rich text and empty plain fallback` / `empty formatted text and empty plain fallback`) or rethrows the 400 from the catch block, surfacing a user-visible delivery failure for content the model never made visible. ## Behavior addressed Interrupted mid-reply turns can produce formatted Telegram HTML that has no visible text and no plain-text fallback, for example an empty supported tag such as ``. Telegram rejects that payload with HTTP 400 (`message text is empty` legacy wording, `text must be non-empty` newer wording). Previously this surfaced as a user-visible delivery failure; this PR silently treats that empty-text send as a no-op with correct accounting. Parse errors remain out of scope and still throw (bare `
` payloads fail as parse errors, per the live baseline below). ## Change - `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` now also matches `text must be non-empty` and the rich-lane `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED` rejection. - `sendTelegramText` returns `Promise`: when the rendered payload is empty and the plain fallback is also empty, it resolves `undefined` (silent no-op) instead of throwing, both pre-flight and when Telegram rejects the payload as empty. Sends with a usable plain fallback still recover exactly as on `main`; parse errors and unrelated failures still throw. - `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` treats an `undefined` chunk result as a no-op: no `markReplyApplied`, no `markDelivered`, so skipped chunks do not advance reply state, delivered count, transcript mirroring, `message_sent.success`, or pinning. - Review fix (clawsweeper finding on the previous revision): in the suppressed single-use multi-chunk lane (the Telegram Desktop workaround in `reply-threading.ts`), the reply target is now consumed on the first delivered chunk instead of being keyed to chunk index 0. Previously a silently-skipped chunk 0 left `progress.hasReplied` false forever, leaking unconsumed single-use reply state to later sends in the same batch that share the delivery progress (`deliverReplies` creates one shared progress per batch). `markReplyApplied` is idempotent, so delivered chunks after the first are no-ops. - Voice fallback text paths mirror only text that actually reached Telegram: an all-skipped caption fallback no longer registers `reply.text` as delivered transcript content. ## Verification Run after this patch on the rebased head (current `main` d3ff48c51f + this commit): ``` node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/reply-threading.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts -> 4 files, 83 tests passed node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram -> 134 files, 2464 tests passed (the pre-rebase bot.test.ts failure noted in the previous revision no longer reproduces on current main) node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json -> clean node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json -> clean oxlint -> clean oxfmt --check -> clean ``` The new regression test (`reply-threading.test.ts`, skipped chunk 0 followed by two delivered chunks) fails on the previous revision with `expected [ false, false, false ] to deeply equal [ false, false, true ]` and passes with the fix; a second case pins that across separate single-chunk sends sharing progress, the reply target attaches to the first delivered send exactly once and skipped sends neither consume nor break the chain. ## Live Telegram round-trip Raw Telegram Bot API baseline (no OpenClaw code), re-run 2026-07-08 against the live Bot API: ``` payload="
" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unsupported start tag \"br\" at byte offset 0" payload="" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: text must be non-empty" payload="OpenClaw PR 88810 raw Bot API baseline: delivered reply" -> ok=true message_id=11323 ``` `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText`, run on the exact rebased head `f5807ad1b2ca2b68c792151f7094b6ad70ddb8cd` against the live Bot API (token and chat id redacted): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) (a) empty html + empty plain fallback -> resolved: undefined [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11324 (b) normal payload -> resolved message_id: 11324 ``` Second `tsx` driver on the same exact head exercising the fixed `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` single-use consumption lane live (chunk 0 renders empty and is skipped by Telegram, chunk 1 delivers, then a follow-up send shares the same delivery progress): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11325 anchor message_id: 11325 [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11326 multi-chunk batch: sendChunk replyToMessageId per chunk: [ undefined, undefined ] progress.hasReplied after skipped chunk 0 + delivered chunk 1: true [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11327 follow-up sendChunk replyToMessageId: [ undefined ] ``` The suppressed multi-chunk lane attaches the native reply param to no chunk by design (Telegram Desktop workaround); the state proof is `progress.hasReplied: true` after the first delivered chunk and the follow-up send not resurrecting the anchor reply target. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Empty visible-text Telegram HTML sends with an empty plain fallback no longer surface as delivery failures; they are treated as no-op sends with no phantom delivery accounting and no leaked single-use reply state, while parse errors and fallback-capable sends behave as on main. Real environment tested: Live Telegram Bot API on the exact rebased head f5807ad1b2ca2b68c792151f7094b6ad70ddb8cd (raw `sendMessage` curl baseline plus a `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText` via grammY), and local Vitest runs of the rebased code. Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/reply-threading.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram`, and the live driver above on the exact head. Evidence after fix: 83/83 tests pass across the four delivery/reply test files, including the new consumption regression (skipped chunk 0 no longer strands `progress.hasReplied`); live Bot API on the exact head resolves `undefined` for `` with `plainText: ""` (logged as a skip, no throw) and returns a real `message_id` (11324) for a normal payload. Observed result after fix: Empty-text sends skip silently without advancing reply delivery state; the single-use reply target is consumed by the first delivered chunk even when earlier chunks skip; payloads with real content or a usable plain fallback deliver unchanged; bare `
` HTML still throws the Telegram parse error and remains out of scope. What was not tested: No full live interrupted-agent session was exercised; the live driver exercises `sendTelegramText` directly rather than the whole `deliverReplies` pipeline over a running gateway. Focused regression tests cover send skipping, reply accounting, single-use reply consumption, transcript mirroring, hooks, pin behavior, and voice fallback paths.

target.title: fix(acp): ACP session startup fails when backend does not advertise thinking config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103802 — ACP sessions can fail at startup with:

```
AcpRuntimeError: ACP backend "acpx" does not accept config key "thinking".: code=ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL
```

This happens when thinking is inherited from defaults/model profile and then applied to a backend that does not advertise a thinking config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch preserves explicit user intent while tolerating inherited defaults only when unsupported:

1. **Track thinking provenance at spawn/init time**
   - `thinkingSource: "explicit" | "default"` is recorded when ACP runtime options are created
   - persisted in ACP session metadata as `runtimeOptionSources.thinking`

2. **Apply strictness by provenance in runtime controls**
   - if backend advertises keys and a thinking key is not supported:
     - `thinkingSource === "default"` → skip (best-effort inherited default)
     - `thinkingSource === "explicit"` (or unknown) → throw `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL` (fail-visible explicit intent)

3. **Sync provenance on mutation paths**
   - `setSessionConfigOption` with a thinking key → sets provenance to "explicit"
   - `updateSessionRuntimeOptions` with thinking in patch → sets provenance to "explicit"
   - `resetSessionRuntimeOptions` → clears provenance

4. **Preserve existing configured/model-profile defaults on capable backends**
   - defaults are still inherited and applied where supported

## User Impact

- ACP sessions against limited backends no longer fail due to inherited default thinking values.
- Explicit `sessions_spawn(thinking: ...)` remains strict and fails visibly when unsupported.
- Changing thinking after spawn (via setConfigOption or updateRuntimeOptions) correctly updates provenance.
- Configured/model-profile thinking defaults still apply on backends that support them.

## Changes Since Last Review

### Rebased onto latest upstream/main
Branch was 50 commits behind and conflicted. Rebased cleanly — all 5 commits applied without semantic conflict.

### Legacy migration added
Added `backfillAcpSessionProvenance()` in `ensureAdditiveStateColumns` — when the new `runtime_option_sources_json` column is added, existing rows with `runtime_options_json` containing `"thinking"` are backfilled with `{"thinking":"default"}`. This ensures pre-patch sessions with inherited thinking are tolerated after upgrade instead of continuing to fail.

### Migration proof
```
=== BEFORE MIGRATION ===
[
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s1", "runtime_options_json": "{\"thinking\":\"high\",\"model\":\"gpt-4\"}" },
  { "session_key": "agent:codex:acp:s2", "runtime_options_json": "{\"model\":\"claude-3\"}" },
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s3", "runtime_options_json": "{\"thinking\":\"high\",\"model\":\"gpt-4\"}" }
]

=== AFTER MIGRATION (backfilled 2 rows) ===
[
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s1", "runtime_options_json": "...", "runtime_option_sources_json": "{\"thinking\":\"default\"}" },
  { "session_key": "agent:codex:acp:s2", "runtime_options_json": "...", "runtime_option_sources_json": null },
  { "session_key": "agent:opencode:acp:s3", "runtime_options_json": "...", "runtime_option_sources_json": "{\"thinking\":\"default\"}" }
]
```
Rows with thinking get backfilled as "default". Rows without thinking stay NULL (correct — no provenance needed).

## Evidence

- 20 files changed, ~320 insertions, ~5 deletions
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main` (commit `8310c565`)
- All tests pass:

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-config.test.ts
✓ 23 passed (including 4 new provenance tests)

$ pnpm vitest run src/acp/runtime/session-meta.test.ts
✓ 9 passed

$ pnpm vitest run src/agents/acp-spawn.test.ts
✓ 66 passed

$ pnpm vitest run src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts
✓ 23 passed
```

- Legacy migration verified: pre-patch rows with `runtime_options_json` containing `"thinking"` are backfilled with `{"thinking":"default"}` on column addition
- Rows without thinking remain NULL (no provenance needed)

target.title: fix(openai): align auth availability with effective routes
target.body:
Closes #103150

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring OpenAI, ChatGPT subscription, custom-endpoint, or routed provider models could see a model reported as available even though the selected credentials could not reach its effective backend, or reported unavailable despite valid route-specific credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider-owned route facts now carry the effective API, endpoint, auth requirement, and prepared credential state through selection, model browsing, runtime execution, compaction, onboarding, doctor, and CLI status. Direct API-key and ChatGPT subscription routes remain distinct; custom endpoints fail closed against incompatible subscription credentials; runtime-only route details stay out of public model-list projections.

## User Impact

OpenAI-family availability and execution now agree across the CLI, Gateway, model catalog, Android inventory consumer, and embedded-agent runtime. Valid resolved SecretRefs and AWS SDK-chain routes are recognized, while credentials for a different backend no longer make an incompatible route appear usable.

## Evidence

- Testbox-through-Crabbox `tbx_01kx9cnxg0hj3p35zc4xfr2js9`: 622 focused tests passed across route auth, catalog visibility, BTW/overflow compaction, Codex auth bridging, startup, shared-client, side-question, and run-attempt behavior.

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.


## Node-host prompt parity (b0164f0fe8a, 2026-07-09)

Review found that the `host=node` `security=full`/`ask=off` fast path invoked `system.run` directly before prepare/approval registration, so a denylist STOP rule hard-denied server-side (`denylist-hit`) instead of raising the documented human allow-once prompt.

Fixed for prompt parity (recommended option):

- The direct fast path is taken only when the caller-visible effective denylist is **known empty**: the `openclaw.json` config layer is empty AND the node approvals-file denylist (fetched via `exec.approvals.node.get`) is known and empty. Fetch failures fail **closed** into the prepare path.
- On the prepare path, the effective denylist (config layer + node approvals-file layer) is evaluated caller-side; a hit forces a registered human approval request even at full/off, mirroring the gateway host: auto-review is excluded (human-only), and `allow-always` is downgraded to one-shot so no durable trust can be minted from a denylist hit.
- Non-matching commands with a configured denylist still auto-run (via the prepare path); setups with no denylist keep the direct fast path.

Focused tests added in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`: config-layer hit registers an approval request (no direct denial), approvals-file hit registers an approval request, non-matching denylist auto-runs, known-empty denylist keeps the fast path, approvals fetch failure fails closed to prepare. `vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts --pool=forks` => 4 files, 146 tests passed; tsgo typecheck clean.

Honest proof status: production decision-function proof and the focused node-host approval-registration tests are in; a live gateway+node prompt -> allow-once -> runs-exactly-once capture is being prepared on a dedicated QA host and will be appended when complete.

Known residual (intentional, documented here): a denylist configured ONLY in the node machine's own local `openclaw.json` remains invisible to the gateway-side caller and still hard-denies server-side (fail-closed). The two operator surfaces this PR documents (`tools.exec.denylist` config layer and the exec-approvals file) now both get prompt parity on host=node.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload
target.body:
## Problem

During an in-process SIGUSR1/config reload, inbound messages can still exist only in debounce buffers or followup queues. Closing the process without flushing those in-memory owners can silently discard accepted message content.

## Fix

This branch is rebuilt on current main as a focused 13-file change.

1. **Close gateway work admission synchronously.** The existing restart request path closes ordinary admission before the drain starts.
2. **Run one core-private restart continuation.** `gateway-work-admission.ts` tracks the restart drain as root work and permits subordinate command work only inside that internal continuation (and required continuations reserved while it is live). Ordinary post-drain enqueue still receives `GatewayDrainingError`.
3. **Flush inbound debounce buffers.** `createInboundDebouncer()` instances are weakly registered. `flushAllInboundDebouncers()` repeatedly sweeps until no live buffer remains, clears each timer, preserves per-key serialization, and does not add teardown requirements to channel implementations.
4. **Drain channel worker queues.** A core-owned registry counts queued and running `ChannelRunQueue` work. The public queue contract remains exactly `enqueue` + `deactivate`; there is no privileged public enqueue method.
5. **Drain active turns, followups, and late followup work in order.** The run loop flushes debouncers, waits for channel queues, lets existing active work settle, waits for every followup queue, then rechecks command/embedded work started by followup delivery.
6. **Count all followup backlog.** `waitForFollowupQueueDrain()` counts `items.length + droppedCount + draining`, so overflow-summary content cannot be reported as drained early.

Explicit forced restarts retain their existing skip-drain behavior.

## Compatibility and security boundary

- Removed the prior `ChannelRunQueue.enqueueInternal` / `allowDuringGatewayDrain` public SDK bypass.
- No `CommandQueueEnqueueOptions` escape hatch is exposed.
- `createInboundDebouncer()` keeps its existing public return signature (`enqueue`, `flushKey`, `cancelKey`); its flush hook is symbol-private.
- `ChannelRunQueue` keeps its existing public shape.
- The branch diff is now 13 focused files (+635/-127), down from the stale 31-file/+1330 version.

## Exact-head validation

- **PR head:** `1952ec24195d85e8f6ea032fe76b44806d952f69`
- **Synchronized main cutoff:** `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`
- **Merge topology:** the cutoff synchronization commit has first parent `da4b1b9c15b6a7b965657fc753e0c25d8dd0e4fa` and second parent `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`.
- Every existing touched main-path blob was re-fetched at the cutoff and verified unchanged from the tested source; the three added paths were verified absent. The 13 changed blobs in the final head are byte-for-byte the locally tested files.
- **Environment:** Linux 6.12.47, Node v24.14.0.

### Runtime behavior proof

A temporary `tsx` driver loaded the changed TypeScript modules directly and exercised real timers, registries, queue work, and command admission:

```text
$ node --import tsx proof-pr46303.mts
debounce {"delivered":[["hello","there"],["howdy"],["ping-1","ping-2"]],"elapsedMs":0,"flushedBuffers":3,"secondSweep":0}
followup {"result":{"drained":true,"remaining":0},"elapsedMs":152}
followup-timeout {"drained":false,"remaining":2}
channel {"pending":{"drained":false,"remaining":1},"drained":{"drained":true,"remaining":0}}
admission {"externalError":"GatewayDrainingError","internalResult":"accepted"}
```

This demonstrates that three 2.5-second debounce buffers flush immediately and only once; a live followup drain waits through `droppedCount` summary backlog; timeout reports the two pending summaries; channel queue accounting observes active work until settlement; and the gateway fence rejects ordinary enqueue while accepting the core-private restart continuation.

### Automated checks

```text
$ vitest run <six focused files>
Test Files  6 passed (6)
Tests       166 passed (166)
Duration    4.35s

$ oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed core files>
(no findings)

$ oxfmt --check <13 changed files>
All matched files use the correct format.

$ run-tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json
passed

$ run-tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json
passed

$ run-tsgo -p tsconfig.plugin-sdk.dts.json --declaration true
passed
```

GitHub Actions is running on the exact head above.

## Not tested

A live Signal account was not paired in this environment, so I did not execute a real Signal → `config.patch` → SIGUSR1 roundtrip. The production restart ordering is covered by `run-loop.test.ts`, and the underlying buffer, queue, admission, and timer behavior was exercised directly as shown above.

target.title: fix(signal): include quoted reply context for agents
target.body:
Closes #98287
Related: #98234 (non-duplicate reply-session initialization conflict/drop issue)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal users sending quoted replies could have the quoted target extracted into `ReplyToBody` metadata while the agent-facing `BodyForAgent` remained only the new ambiguous message, such as `Did this get done?`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now renders visible quoted-reply context directly into `BodyForAgent` as a clear blockquote while preserving clean `RawBody`, `CommandBody`, and `BodyForCommands` for command parsing and hooks. The shared inbound metadata renderer skips only the duplicate one-hop reply-target block when the Signal-generated wrapper exactly matches the expected quoted body and sender; richer `ReplyChain` context and ordinary user-authored blockquotes still render normally.

## User Impact

Signal quoted replies now carry the referenced message into agent-facing input, so agents can answer ambiguous followups using the intended quoted target. Plain non-quoted Signal messages remain unchanged, and quoted context is not duplicated in the model prompt when Signal has already inlined the generated quote block.

## Evidence

Duplicate search before filing found no open narrow issue/PR for `Signal quoted reply BodyForAgent` / `agent-facing body`; the closest existing items were closed #68665 and related-but-different #84364, plus broad open quote-reply PRs that do not provide this narrow BodyForAgent fix.

Validation run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/signal/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo && node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src` (29 files, 375 tests)
- `git diff --check`
- Exact-head regression coverage now canonicalizes blank lines in multi-paragraph quoted text (`>` with no trailing space) and proves the duplicate metadata block stays suppressed.
- Debounced Signal batches now render reply context per entry before joining the batch, with quoted-first/plain-last and plain-first/quoted-last regressions and an internal exact-once marker that preserves the last structured reply metadata without duplicating it in the prompt.
- Fresh GitHub CI is running after the only preceding failure—two formatter-only line wraps in the Signal handler—was fixed on exact head `8087d6f852d51bf20dd0bca1d13c900219d6e3ed`, which includes the shared upstream cutoff `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --prompt 'Review the final Signal quoted-reply BodyForAgent change after exact generated-prefix duplicate checks that include expected sender and boundary. Confirm no accepted duplicate-context, equal-body, spoofed marker/altered wrapper, ReplyChain, or command/raw body regressions remain.'` clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

Caveat: no live Signal device roundtrip was run in this isolated checkout. The proof is source-level focused tests, the full Signal plugin Vitest directory, TypeScript checks, format/whitespace checks, and autoreview.

AI-assisted implementation; no agent transcript is included because this task involved private Signal context and the local transcript prompt flow was unavailable in this run mode.

target.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings
target.body:
## Summary

- Rebases PR #94344 onto current main and resolves the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider conflicts without changing the intended SSRF contract.
- Updates the added SSRF tests to match the exported `LookupFn` overload shape.
- Updates the memory config docs to describe exact configured `baseUrl` hostname trust, not origin trust.
- Prevents configured local-service acquisition and health probes when the selected provider explicitly sets `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false`.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Operators using configured OpenAI-compatible memory embedding providers need the selected provider's private-endpoint policy to behave predictably: omitted policy preserves exact configured origin compatibility, explicit `false` fails closed, and explicit `true` allows broader private-network access.
- **Scope boundary:** The rebase repair changes only the existing embedding SSRF policy integration, its tests/docs, and the local-service composition needed to honor explicit denial before any probe. It does not change schema, migrations, non-memory provider request paths, gateway/channel/session routing, global SSRF helpers, dependencies, or lockfiles.

Fixes #94166

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — existing PR author repair for #94344.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #94180 (`feat(memory-core): allow private network endpoints for memory embeddings`). The public-contract helper also flagged #92307 through an environment/version term, but #92307 is about exec-approval startup warnings and is not the same embedding/private-network contract.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #94180 adds a memory-specific config surface, `memorySearch.remote.network.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork`, for a trust decision that the selected model provider can already express with `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork`.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This PR reuses the existing provider transport-trust contract as the canonical source of truth for configured providers instead of introducing a second memory-only knob. This update only repairs the review findings on that existing approach.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The current-head bounded proof exercises the real `memory status --deep --json` CLI path against a loopback/private OpenAI-compatible daemon backed by the actual FastEmbed `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model. Omitted policy succeeds through exact-origin trust with one `/v1/embeddings` request, explicit `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false` is blocked before the daemon receives any request, and explicit `true` succeeds with one `/v1/embeddings` request.
- **Related open PR scan:** Current same-contract scan found #94180 as the linked alternative for memory private endpoint support; no broader canonical provider-inheritance PR was found besides this PR. #92307 was an environment/version false-positive and is not part of this embedding/private-network contract.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `openclaw memory status --deep` against a configured OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint on a loopback/private address must preserve exact-origin compatibility when provider private-network policy is omitted, must block when the selected provider explicitly sets `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false`, and must honor `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` for explicit broader private-network trust.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User `models.providers.<id>` and `agents.defaults.memorySearch` config → existing config schema/type parsing and configured-provider normalization → `ConfiguredEmbeddingProvider.request.allowPrivateNetwork` on the runtime embedding client → shared SSRF policy → guarded `/v1/embeddings` request or pre-request block.
- **Boundary crossed:** Full config-to-request local runtime path through the real `openclaw memory status --deep --json` CLI and `memory-core` embedding probe into a real FastEmbed model daemon. This is local-daemon behavior proof, not third-party provider proof.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused the repository shared `ssrfPolicyFromHttpBaseUrlAllowedHostname` helper and `resolvePinnedHostnameWithPolicy` test seam. No numeric-string parser or provider-owned range constraint is added or changed; the only provider contract consumed is the existing boolean `request.allowPrivateNetwork` setting.
- **Real environment tested:** CLI behavior proof was captured in the local PR worktree on Linux, using the real source CLI, the real `memory-core` CLI command, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and an OpenAI-compatible FastEmbed `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` daemon bound to a loopback/private address. The proof is bound to current HEAD by daily-fix's non-mock live-proof receipt. Current-head re-verification also covered the rebased runtime integration, test typing, docs wording, and the explicit-denial plus configured-local-service combination.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** The live runtime proof command used for the PR behavior was:

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs memory status --agent proof --deep --json
```

The current rebased head was re-verified with these commands from `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-94344`:

```sh
pnpm exec tsc --ignoreConfig --strict --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --target ES2022 --types node --noEmit /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-94344-evidence/lookupfn-overload-smoke.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts
pnpm check:test-types
git diff --check
```

- **Evidence after fix:** Exact-origin compatibility result from the real CLI, with provider `request.allowPrivateNetwork` omitted:

```json
{
  "agentId": "proof",
  "status": {
    "provider": "openai-compatible",
    "requestedProvider": "private-embedding-proof",
    "model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"
  },
  "embeddingProbe": {
    "ok": true
  }
}
```

Exact-origin compatibility summary:

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "containsEmbeddingsReady": true,
  "serverRequestCount": 1
}
```

Explicit provider denial result from the real CLI:

```json
{
  "agentId": "proof",
  "status": {
    "provider": "openai-compatible",
    "requestedProvider": "private-embedding-proof",
    "model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"
  },
  "embeddingProbe": {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address"
  }
}
```

Explicit provider denial summary:

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "containsGuardBlock": true,
  "containsEmbeddingsReady": false,
  "serverRequestCount": 0
}
```

Provider opt-in overlay result from the real CLI:

```json
{
  "agentId": "proof",
  "status": {
    "provider": "openai-compatible",
    "requestedProvider": "private-embedding-proof",
    "model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"
  },
  "embeddingProbe": {
    "ok": true
  }
}
```

Provider opt-in overlay summary:

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "containsEmbeddingsReady": true,
  "serverRequestCount": 1
}
```

Bound current-head daemon proof summary:

```json
{
  "head": "7f3916ffca66cfab7ecd7d19ee5e6a746b126d86",
  "target": "FastEmbed BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 local embedding daemon",
  "omitted": { "code": 0, "ready": true, "request_count": 1 },
  "explicit_false": { "code": 0, "ready": false, "blocked": true, "request_count": 0 },
  "explicit_true": { "code": 0, "ready": true, "request_count": 1 },
  "embedding_dimension": 384,
  "passed": true
}
```

Current-head review repair verification:

```text
LookupFn overload smoke: passed with no TypeScript diagnostics.
openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 35 passed (35), including configured localService plus explicit private-network denial.
pnpm check:test-types: completed with exit code 0 after rebase; after the final localService denial guard, fresh `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both exited 0.
git diff --check: passed.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The omitted configured provider alias reaches the loopback/private embedding endpoint successfully. The explicit false config is blocked by the guarded-fetch path before the endpoint sees a request. The explicit true config returns `embeddingProbe.ok: true` and reaches the endpoint once. The current update also resolves the `LookupFn` overload type issue and keeps the provider test passing under the owning Vitest config.
- **What was not tested:** I did not use a maintainer's real private LAN/VPN embedding service, third-party credentials, Mantis, Telegram, or Desktop proof infrastructure. This PR does not touch Telegram/Desktop/channel delivery; the local proof exercises the relevant memory CLI, configured-provider, and guarded-fetch runtime surface. I did not drive a live metadata/link-local endpoint for safety; metadata/link-local rebinding remains covered by the exact-origin regression test that resolves the configured hostname to `169.254.169.254` and expects private/internal blocking when broader opt-in is not set. I did not run `openclaw memory index --force`; `memory status --deep` is the requested memory runtime probe path and reaches the embedding availability check directly.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix plus author-side review repair.

## Review findings addressed

| Finding | Status | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RF-001 | Addressed | This author update responds to the current `status: ⏳ waiting on author` state. Label removal still depends on the next ClawSweeper/maintainer pass after submission. |
| RF-002 | Disclosed/maintainer decision | Explicit `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false` intentionally fails closed for configured private endpoints that previously depended on omitted-policy exact-origin trust. The docs and three-state proof make that upgrade-sensitive behavior explicit rather than silently preserving unsafe compatibility. |
| RF-003 | Disclosed/maintainer decision | The omitted/false/true SSRF contract remains a maintainer/security-boundary decision. This contributor update implements and proves the requested behavior but does not present that policy choice as independently approved. |
| RF-004 | Fixed within scope / disclosed | Fresh isolated configs were exercised for omitted, explicit false, and explicit true. The resolver receives only `{ allowPrivateNetwork }`; unrelated configured auth, proxy, and TLS fields are deliberately excluded, so existing embedding base URL, header, API-key, proxy, and TLS construction is unchanged. A real upgrade from a maintainer deployment with custom auth/proxy/TLS was not exercised and remains disclosed below. |
| RF-005 | Fixed/proven | Replaced the adapter-local private-network decision with `resolveProviderRequestPolicyConfig`, narrowed the resolver request input to `allowPrivateNetwork` only, and repeated the full three-state CLI proof against the real FastEmbed daemon. |
| RF-006 | Fixed/proven | The embedding client now calls the canonical provider request resolver with provider id, API, normalized base URL, `capability: "other"`, `transport: "http"`, and an `allowPrivateNetwork`-only request object. A failing-first integration test includes unrelated auth, proxy, and TLS fields and proves they are not forwarded. |
| RF-007 | Fixed/proven | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts src/agents/provider-request-config.test.ts` passed; the provider suite reports 36/36 tests. |
| RF-008 | Fixed/proven | `pnpm check:test-types` completed successfully across core-test, extensions-test, and test-root. |
| RF-009 | Fixed/proven | `git diff --check` completed with no output, and oxfmt reports both changed TypeScript files correctly formatted. |
| RF-010 | Fixed/proven | Repeated the requested redacted `memory status --agent proof --deep --json` runtime proof for all three policy states against the real FastEmbed model daemon: omitted succeeded with one embedding POST, explicit `false` was blocked with zero health probes and zero embedding POSTs, and explicit `true` succeeded with one embedding POST. The bound summary is `live-proof/fastembed-current-head.json`, with its daily-fix live-proof receipt alongside it. |

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`
- **Target files:** `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`; `docs/reference/memory-config.md`
- **Scenario locked in:** Configured OpenAI-compatible memory providers use the selected provider request policy: omitted policy keeps exact configured `baseUrl` origin trust, explicit `false` opts out of exact-origin private-network trust, and explicit `true` allows broader private-network embedding requests. Different ports, protocols, and redirect origins remain blocked without explicit broader opt-in; private/internal resolution also remains blocked when broader opt-in is not set.
- **Commands run after this author repair:**

```sh
pnpm exec tsc --ignoreConfig --strict --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --target ES2022 --types node --noEmit /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-94344-evidence/lookupfn-overload-smoke.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts
pnpm check:test-types
git diff --check
```

- **Observed local result:** The `LookupFn` overload smoke passed without TypeScript diagnostics; `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts` passed 35/35 tests under `test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts`; full post-rebase `pnpm check:test-types` exited 0, then fresh `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both exited 0 after the final localService denial guard; `git diff --check` exited 0.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The rebase keeps the existing provider-policy helper and adds one composition guard so explicit denial is enforced before local-service acquisition. The owning provider test locks the combined path without expanding unrelated provider or gateway coverage.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** security-boundary, compatibility, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** The PR touches the security boundary for private-network embedding fetches and the provider/config contract that decides when exact-origin or broader private-network trust is allowed. A wrong change could relax SSRF blocking by default, carry trust across ports/protocols/redirects, break existing configured local/private aliases, or create a second incompatible memory-only trust surface.
- **Why acceptable:** The PR's runtime behavior remains constrained to the canonical provider policy: omitted config preserves only the exact configured origin, explicit false denies that exact-origin trust and also prevents local-service probes, and explicit true is required for broader private-network access.
- **What did NOT change:** No schema, migration, new config key, provider parser/range, global SSRF helper, non-memory provider transport, gateway/channel/session routing, dependency, lockfile, or unrelated cleanup changed. The test-only `as unknown as` casts adapt partial config and overloaded `LookupFn` fixtures; the canonical config-to-request reachability is separately exercised through the real CLI path above.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The original issue is that memory-core OpenAI-compatible embeddings did not consistently consume the selected configured provider's `request.allowPrivateNetwork` policy when building the embedding SSRF policy. During rebase, current main's configured local-service acquisition path composed ahead of guarded fetch, so explicit denial could still trigger a private health probe before the embedding POST was blocked. The adapter also continued reading the boolean directly after current main introduced the canonical provider request resolver, creating a second policy decision path.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The embedding client now obtains `allowPrivateNetwork` and `privateNetworkExplicitlyDenied` from `resolveProviderRequestPolicyConfig`, passes only the policy field it consumes, uses that one result for both SSRF policy and local-service acquisition, and preserves existing header/auth/proxy/TLS/base URL construction. It does not add downstream fetch fallbacks, a parallel memory-only knob, or unrelated runtime changes.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix with focused author repair.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical contract surface is `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork` for configured provider transport trust. Memory embedding SSRF policy consumes that provider-owned request setting; this PR does not add a parallel `memorySearch` private-network knob, does not change schema/default values, and does not alter unrelated provider, gateway, channel, or session contracts.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** Medium-high — local CLI proof exists for the runtime path, the current author repair passes focused and full test-type verification, and the remaining SSRF/private-network acceptance is disclosed as maintainer/security judgment rather than presented as already externally approved.
- **Patch quality notes:** The `as unknown as LookupFn` casts are test-only fixtures for the overloaded `dns.promises.lookup` signature and match the existing SSRF pinning test pattern; the `EmbeddingProviderCreateOptions["config"]` casts are partial canonical config fixtures, not production type suppression. The runtime `return undefined` for explicit false is the intentional provider-denial path, and the local-service guard prevents any pre-guard probe under that same canonical config. No skipped tests, `.only`, lint disables, runtime catch-all fallback, schema migration, or new public config knob were added.

target.title: fix(telegram): prevent unlisted API calls from stalling delivery
target.body:
Closes #104524

AI-assisted: yes. I used an OpenAI coding agent, reviewed the resulting change, and understand the timeout behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users could have all outbound replies for a session stall for roughly eight minutes when an API call used a method that was not explicitly listed in the client timeout table.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every identified Telegram API method except `getUpdates` now receives the existing 60-second outbound timeout as a default. Explicit method-specific guards remain unchanged, higher configured timeouts are still honored, and requests whose method cannot be identified remain untouched.

## User Impact

A newly introduced or otherwise unlisted Telegram API method can no longer silently fall back to grammY's approximately 500-second timeout and park the serialized delivery lane. Its client-side guard defaults to 60 seconds unless the operator configured a higher timeout.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 1 file, 15 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension telegram` — 142 files, 2,666 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.ts extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.ts extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — formatting passed.
- `NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=2300' node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/telegram/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

No live Telegram probe was run because this checkout has no test-bot credentials. The linked issue includes the production incident evidence and reports the same fallback behavior running in production.

### Controlled runtime proof

A credential-free controlled Bot API endpoint exercised the real `createTelegramClientFetch` and `AbortController` path on this PR branch. All three requests ran concurrently against delayed local HTTP responses; no Telegram token or external API was used.

```text
controlled_endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>/bot<redacted>/METHOD
unlisted-default: answerCallbackQuery, server delay 65000ms -> aborted after 60004ms: Telegram answercallbackquery timed out after 60000ms
unlisted-configured-override: answerCallbackQuery, configured timeout 70s, server delay 62000ms -> HTTP 200 after 62030ms
getUpdates-unchanged: getUpdates, configured timeout 70s, server delay 65000ms -> aborted after 45015ms: Telegram getupdates timed out after 45000ms
proof_result=PASS
```

This demonstrates the 60-second fallback through the actual fetch wrapper, the existing higher configured-timeout escape hatch, and the unchanged 45-second `getUpdates` guard.
